title: Keep the analyzer working when source generation is suppressed

lines.text: > Note: When using Unity, dynamic code generation only works when targeting .NET Framework 4.x + mono runtime.
For all other Unity targets, AOT is required.
A `[MessagePackObject]` type can opt out of source generation with `[MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)]`.
No formatter is generated for that type. It is serialized at run time by the dynamic resolvers, which use reflection, so such a type is not AOT-safe.
The analyzer still validates these types, because they are serialized at run time and must still have a valid contract:
- Keys are unique and all of the same kind ([MsgPack005](doc/analyzers/MsgPack005.md)).
- Members have types that are themselves serializable ([MsgPack003](doc/analyzers/MsgPack003.md)).
- Types are accessible to the resolver ([MsgPack012](doc/analyzers/MsgPack012.md)).

The analyzer does not report the partial-class requirement ([MsgPack011](doc/analyzers/MsgPack011.md)) or the AOT-only checks ([MsgPack016](doc/analyzers/MsgPack016.md) and [MsgPack017](doc/analyzers/MsgPack017.md)) for these types, because they only apply when a formatter is generated.
You can customize the generated source through properties on the `GeneratedMessagePackResolverAttribute`.

requirement.title: The analyzer does not work if SuppressSourceGeneration = true
requirement.intent: The analyzer must report its diagnostics for types that set SuppressSourceGeneration = true, as it did in version 3.1.0.

functional.text: The analyzer reports diagnostics for a [MessagePackObject] type with SuppressSourceGeneration = true.
The analyzer behaves for such types as it did in version 3.1.0, before the regression in 3.1.1.

nonFunctional.text: The analyzer must not crash on invalid input in a suppressed type; it reports the problem instead. (inferred)
Types that do not suppress source generation keep their current diagnostics. (inferred)

expectedBehaviours: Compiling a project with a [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] type that breaks a rule, such as a public member without a [Key] attribute, produces the matching MsgPack diagnostic in the build output.
The diagnostic appears in the IDE and in command-line builds even though the generator emits no formatter for that type.
Diagnostics point at the right location (member or type) in the suppressed type.

An analyzer test with a suppressed type that has duplicate or mixed key styles expects the matching diagnostic.

expectedBehaviours: For suppressed types, the set of diagnostic IDs, severities and locations matches what version 3.1.0 reported for the same source.
Rules that applied to suppressed types in 3.1.0 apply again. Rules that 3.1.0 skipped for suppressed types are not newly reported.

story.what: The change hardens TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo so that invalid key setups no longer throw. After reporting a mixed int/string key diagnostic, it now skips that member (continue). It also adds a member to intMembers or stringMembers only if the key is not already there, so duplicate keys no longer call Dictionary.Add twice. It also tightens the condition for flushing deferred non-public-member diagnostics from || to &&. A README section documents how the analyzer treats SuppressSourceGeneration types, and new analyzer and execution tests cover suppressed types.
story.why: Since 3.1.1 the analyzer stopped reporting diagnostics for [MessagePackObject(SuppressSourceGeneration = true)] types (issue 2234). In the code, the analyzer path for these types could throw on duplicate or mixed keys: Dictionary.Add with a duplicate key, or intKey!.Value on a null value. That would abort analysis instead of reporting diagnostics. The change makes the collector report the problem and keep going, so suppressed types get their diagnostics again.

touches.note: Skips members with a mismatched key kind, guards dictionary adds against duplicate keys, and changes the condition for reporting deferred diagnostics to && with AllowPrivate.
New analyzer tests for suppressed types: MsgPack004/015/003/005 are reported, and the source-generation-only diagnostics are not.
New execution tests: no generated formatter for a suppressed type, and a round trip through the dynamic resolver.
New docs section listing which analyzer rules apply to suppressed types.

findings.title: Deferred non-public member diagnostics now need both conditions
findings.detail: In hunk h8 the condition for reporting deferred diagnostics for non-public members changed from (nonPublicMembersAreSerialized || allowPrivateAttribute is true) to (nonPublicMembersAreSerialized && allowPrivateAttribute is true). The requirement does not ask for this, and it applies to all types, suppressed or not. Case 1: a type without AllowPrivate that has a private keyed member no longer gets MsgPack004 for its other private members that have no key; only MsgPack015 remains. Case 2: a type with AllowPrivate = true and no private keyed member no longer gets MsgPack004 for private members that have no key. Those members are then not serialized at run time and nothing warns about it. This breaks N2 (non-suppressed types keep their diagnostics) and F2 (the 3.1.0 behaviour), and no test covers the change.

findings.title: A null key on the first field still crashes the analyzer
findings.detail: N1 requires the analyzer to report invalid input instead of crashing. In the field loop, a first keyed field with [Key(null)] reports BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull and sets isIntKey to false. Execution then reaches the bare else branch, which calls stringMembers.ContainsKey(stringKey!) with a null key. That throws ArgumentNullException, which shows up as AD0001 instead of a diagnostic. The property loop is protected by 'else if (stringKey is not null)', but the field loop is not. The new ContainsKey guards in h6 and h7 do not cover this case, and no test uses a null key.
